title: Everybody panic: A Valve developer said "HLX" in public
gist: At a GameSoundCon panel, Valve composer Mike Morasky mentioned that "HLX", the widely reported internal codename for Valve's next Half-Life project, has its own version of Valve's HDR audio system, the first public reference to it by a Valve employee. The Steam Machine launched without the Half-Life 3 tie-in that journalist Mike Straw had predicted, and Valve watcher Tyler McVicker no longer expects an HLX announcement this calendar year, although he points to rising Valve commit activity.

themes.theme: First public HLX reference from Valve staff

insights.claim: During a GameSoundCon panel on Valve's open audio engines, Valve composer Mike Morasky said that HLX has its own version of the company's high dynamic range (HDR) audio system, as Deadlock does.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Implies a Half-Life project is in active enough development to have its own audio pipeline.
insights.quote: I think Deadlock has their own version of HDR. HLX has its own version, so on and so forth

insights.claim: HLX is widely reported to be the internal codename for Valve's next Half-Life project; it has appeared in Valve engine code since at least 2024 but had never been referenced in public by a Valve employee until Morasky's remark.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Moves the signal from data-mined code strings to a statement by an insider.
insights.locator: “HLX,” of course, has been widely reported

insights.claim: Just under a year ago, journalist Mike Straw insisted Half-Life 3 would be a Steam Machine launch title, but the Steam Machine launched without even a hint of an announcement, making Valve watchers wary of new rumors.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: A failed prediction tied to a hardware launch means release-timing rumors should be discounted.
insights.locator: Remember, it was just under a year ago

insights.claim: Valve watcher Tyler McVicker, who said last year that Half-Life 3 was in its final stages of development and a 2026 announcement was likely, now says he does not expect HLX to be announced this calendar year.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Pushes the expected announcement window into 2027 or later.

insights.claim: Fellow panelist and Valve sound designer David Feise appeared to react to the slip, mumbling a sarcastic "nice work" and later saying "Good job—you only said HLX once!"
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: His reaction suggests the codename was not meant to be public, which adds to its credibility.
insights.quote: Good job—you only said HLX once!
insights.locator: In the panel video, fellow panelist

insights.claim: McVicker also points to recently increased Valve coding activity, measured by externally visible internal commit counts, as a sign something big may come sooner rather than later.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Commit activity is an outside proxy that watchers use to track Valve's development cycles.
insights.locator: But he also pointed to recently increased

insights.claim: Orland argues that whenever Half-Life 3 arrives, it will have to be truly incredible to make up for losing the long-running metagame of speculating about whether it exists.
insights.speaker: Kyle Orland
insights.so_what: Expectations are extremely high, which adds launch risk for any eventual release.
